questions.stem: An organism that manufactures its own organic food from simple inorganic substances is described as
questions.explanation: Autotrophs build organic molecules such as glucose from carbon dioxide and water, using either light energy (photosynthesis) or energy from chemical reactions (chemosynthesis). All other modes listed depend on organic food that another organism has already made.

distractorRationale.a: Heterotrophs depend on ready-made organic food
distractorRationale.c: Saprophytes are a kind of heterotroph that feeds on dead organic matter
distractorRationale.d: Parasites are heterotrophs that take food from a living host

questions.stem: Rhizopus growing on stale bread secretes enzymes onto the bread and absorbs the digested products. This mode of nutrition is
questions.explanation: The bread is dead organic matter and digestion happens outside the fungus before absorption, which is exactly what defines saprophytic nutrition. Saprophytes are the decomposers that release nutrients back into the soil.

distractorRationale.a: Holozoic feeders take solid food into a gut and digest it internally
distractorRationale.b: A parasite feeds on a living host and harms it; bread is not alive
distractorRationale.d: Chemosynthesis is a form of autotrophic nutrition, and Rhizopus makes no food of its own

questions.stem: Rhizobium bacteria live in the root nodules of cowpea. The bacteria supply the plant with fixed nitrogen and receive carbohydrates in return. This relationship is
questions.explanation: Both partners gain: the plant obtains nitrogen compounds it could not make from atmospheric nitrogen, and the bacteria obtain sugars from photosynthesis. Mutual benefit with neither partner harmed is the definition of symbiosis, and it is why legumes improve soil fertility.

distractorRationale.a: In parasitism one partner is harmed, but the cowpea benefits
distractorRationale.c: Saprophytism involves feeding on dead matter, and the root is alive
distractorRationale.d: Predation involves killing and eating another organism

questions.stem: Which deficiency disease results from a lack of iodine in the diet?
questions.explanation: Iodine is needed by the thyroid gland to manufacture thyroxine. Without it the gland enlarges as it works harder, producing the visible neck swelling called goitre; this is why table salt is iodised.

distractorRationale.b: Rickets is caused by a shortage of vitamin D or calcium
distractorRationale.c: Scurvy is caused by a shortage of vitamin C
distractorRationale.d: Beriberi is caused by a shortage of vitamin B1, thiamine

questions.stem: A two-year-old child fed almost entirely on garri and pap has a swollen abdomen, wasted limbs and discoloured hair. The most appropriate correction to the diet is to add
questions.explanation: The symptoms describe kwashiorkor, which arises when energy intake is adequate but protein is severely lacking. Beans, groundnut and crayfish are affordable local protein sources that supply the amino acids needed to rebuild tissue and correct the oedema.

distractorRationale.a: Garri and rice are starchy foods; adding more repeats the very imbalance that caused the disease
distractorRationale.c: Palm oil supplies energy and vitamin A but almost no protein
distractorRationale.d: Iodised salt prevents goitre, which is a different deficiency

questions.stem: Roughage is an important part of the diet even though it is not digested. Its main function is to

options.text: add bulk that stimulates peristalsis and prevents constipation
form haemoglobin in red blood cells

questions.explanation: Roughage is mainly cellulose, which human enzymes cannot break down. It stays in the gut as bulk that the muscular wall can grip, keeping peristalsis regular so that faeces pass out easily.

distractorRationale.a: Humans cannot digest cellulose, so no energy is obtained from it
distractorRationale.b: Amino acids come from protein, not from fibre
distractorRationale.d: Haemoglobin formation requires iron and protein

questions.stem: A pitcher plant that traps and digests insects should be classified as a heterotroph.
questions.explanation: False. The pitcher plant is green and makes all its own carbohydrate by photosynthesis, so it is an autotroph. It digests insects only to obtain nitrogen and mineral salts, which are scarce in the marshy soils where it grows.

questions.stem: A farmer complains that he cannot see clearly at dusk although his daytime vision is normal. Which food should be added to his diet?

options.text: Red palm oil and dark green leafy vegetables

questions.explanation: Poor vision in dim light is night blindness, caused by a shortage of vitamin A, which the retina needs to make the pigment rhodopsin. Red palm oil and dark green leaves are rich in carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.

distractorRationale.a: Citrus fruits supply vitamin C, which prevents scurvy rather than night blindness
distractorRationale.c: Rice and cassava are energy foods with negligible vitamin A
distractorRationale.d: Sugar supplies energy only and contains no vitamins

questions.stem: Mistletoe grows on the branches of a cocoa tree, has green leaves of its own but sends root-like structures into the host's xylem. It is best described as
questions.explanation: Because it is green it photosynthesises and makes its own carbohydrate, but it taps the host's xylem for water and mineral salts, which harms the host. Depending on the host for only some requirements makes it a partial, or semi, parasite.

distractorRationale.a: A complete parasite such as dodder has no chlorophyll and takes everything from the host
distractorRationale.c: A saprophyte feeds on dead matter, whereas the cocoa tree is alive
distractorRationale.d: In symbiosis both partners benefit, but the cocoa tree is damaged

questions.stem: Explain what is meant by a balanced diet and state, with reasons, two ways in which the diet of a pregnant woman should differ from that of an office clerk of the same age.
markingGuide: Balanced diet defined as one containing all the food classes — carbohydrate, protein, fat, vitamins, mineral salts, water and roughage — in the correct proportions for the individual's age, sex, body size and occupation (3 marks)
Difference 1: more protein, because amino acids are needed to build the tissues of the developing foetus as well as maintain the mother (2 marks)
Difference 2: more calcium and vitamin D for the bones and teeth of the foetus, or more iron to make the extra haemoglobin required by the increased blood volume and to prevent anaemia (2 marks)
Reason correctly linked to the nutrient in each case rather than merely naming the nutrient (1 mark)
questions.explanation: A balanced diet is defined by proportion as well as by content, which is why requirements differ between individuals. Pregnancy raises the demand for protein for foetal tissue growth and for iron and calcium to support the increased blood volume and skeletal development of the foetus.

questions.stem: The primary source of energy for autotrophic organisms comes from which of the following?
questions.explanation: Autotrophic organisms, such as plants, utilize sunlight as their primary energy source to convert inorganic substances into organic food through the process of photosynthesis. This is a fundamental characteristic that distinguishes them from heterotrophs, which obtain energy from consuming organic matter.

distractorRationale.a: Inorganic compounds are utilized by autotrophs but do not provide energy directly.
distractorRationale.b: Organic compounds are the end products of autotrophic processes, not the source of energy.
distractorRationale.d: Heterotrophs obtain energy from other organisms, not autotrophs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a function of carbohydrates in the diet?

options.text: Serving as a source of dietary fiber

questions.explanation: Carbohydrates primarily serve as a source of energy and contribute to dietary fiber, but they do not play a direct role in muscle building. Proteins are the macronutrients responsible for muscle repair and growth.

distractorRationale.a: Carbohydrates are the main energy source in the diet.
distractorRationale.c: Carbohydrates help in regulating blood sugar levels.
distractorRationale.d: Dietary fiber, derived from carbohydrates, aids in digestion.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes saprophytic nutrition?

options.text: Absorbing nutrients from decaying organic matter

questions.explanation: Saprophytic nutrition involves organisms that feed on dead and decaying organic matter, breaking it down and recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem. This mode of nutrition is crucial for the decomposition process.

distractorRationale.a: Feeding on living hosts describes parasitic nutrition.
distractorRationale.c: Symbiotic relationships involve mutual benefit, not saprophytic feeding.
distractorRationale.d: Photosynthesis is a characteristic of autotrophic nutrition.

questions.explanation: Vitamin A is essential for maintaining healthy vision, particularly in low light conditions. A deficiency in this vitamin can lead to night blindness, highlighting its critical role in visual health.

distractorRationale.b: Vitamin B12 deficiency leads to anemia, not night blindness.
distractorRationale.c: Vitamin C is important for immune function and skin health.
distractorRationale.d: Vitamin D deficiency affects bone health, not night vision.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of parasitic nutrition?

options.text: One organism benefits at the expense of another
Nutrients are absorbed from the soil

questions.explanation: Parasitic nutrition is characterized by one organism benefiting while harming another. The parasite derives nutrients from its host, often causing detriment to the host's health.

distractorRationale.a: This describes mutualism, not parasitism.
distractorRationale.c: Absorption from the soil is typical of autotrophic organisms.
distractorRationale.d: Photosynthesis is a feature of autotrophic nutrition.

questions.stem: Which of the following food classes is primarily responsible for growth and repair of tissues?
questions.explanation: Proteins are essential macronutrients that play a crucial role in the growth and repair of tissues in the body. They are made up of amino acids, which are the building blocks necessary for cellular structure and function.

distractorRationale.a: Carbohydrates mainly provide energy, not tissue repair.
distractorRationale.b: Fats serve as energy storage and insulation.
distractorRationale.d: Vitamins support various bodily functions but do not directly build tissues.

questions.explanation: Dietary fiber is a crucial component of a healthy diet as it aids in digestion by promoting bowel regularity and preventing constipation. It also contributes to overall gut health.

distractorRationale.a: Fiber does not provide energy as it is not digested.
distractorRationale.c: Muscle building is primarily the role of proteins.
distractorRationale.d: While fiber can help regulate blood sugar, its main function is digestive.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common deficiency disease caused by a lack of vitamin C?
questions.explanation: Scurvy is a disease caused by a deficiency of vitamin C, which is essential for collagen synthesis and immune function. Symptoms include fatigue, swollen gums, and joint pain.

distractorRationale.b: Rickets is caused by a deficiency of vitamin D.
distractorRationale.c: Beriberi results from a lack of vitamin B1 (thiamine).
distractorRationale.d: Pellagra is associated with a deficiency of niacin (vitamin B3).

questions.stem: Which of the following is a feature of symbiotic nutrition?

options.text: One organism benefits while the other is harmed
Both organisms benefit from the relationship
Nutrients are absorbed from decaying matter
One organism is autotrophic and the other is heterotrophic

questions.explanation: Symbiotic nutrition occurs when two organisms live together and both benefit from the relationship. This mutualistic interaction can enhance survival and resource acquisition for both parties involved.

distractorRationale.a: This describes parasitism, not symbiosis.
distractorRationale.c: That is characteristic of saprophytic nutrition.
distractorRationale.d: This describes a mixed relationship, not necessarily symbiotic.

questions.stem: Which of the following vitamins is essential for the absorption of calcium in the body?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D is crucial for the absorption of calcium and phosphorus in the body, which are essential for maintaining healthy bones and teeth. A deficiency can lead to conditions such as rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

distractorRationale.a: Vitamin A is important for vision but not calcium absorption.
distractorRationale.b: Vitamin B12 is vital for red blood cell production.
distractorRationale.c: Vitamin C supports immune function and collagen synthesis.

distractorRationale.c: Vitamins support bodily functions but do not provide energy.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes heterotrophic nutrition?

options.text: The process of synthesizing food from sunlight.
The absorption of pre-formed organic compounds.
The conversion of carbon dioxide into glucose.
The use of inorganic substances for food production.

questions.explanation: Heterotrophic nutrition involves organisms obtaining their food by consuming other organisms or organic matter. Unlike autotrophs, heterotrophs cannot produce their own food and rely on external sources for nourishment.

distractorRationale.a: This describes autotrophic nutrition.
distractorRationale.c: This is a characteristic of photosynthesis in autotrophs.
distractorRationale.d: This describes the process of autotrophic nutrition.

distractorRationale.c: Fats provide energy but are not primarily composed of sugars and starches.

questions.stem: What type of relationship exists when one organism benefits at the expense of another?
questions.explanation: Parasitism is a type of feeding relationship where one organism, the parasite, benefits at the expense of the host, which is harmed in the process. This relationship can lead to various health issues in the host.

distractorRationale.a: Mutualism benefits both organisms involved.
distractorRationale.b: Commensalism benefits one organism without affecting the other.
distractorRationale.d: Saprophytism involves feeding on dead organic matter.

distractorRationale.a: Vitamin A is important for vision.
distractorRationale.b: Vitamin B12 is essential for red blood cell production.
distractorRationale.d: Vitamin D is important for calcium absorption.
